title: LTS-aware Validation Gateway: Orchestrate smoke, perf, and eval shadowing for safe upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a validation gateway that is LTS-channel aware and can orchestrate a set of preflight checks (smoke tests, perf regression gates, and full eval suites) using traffic shadowing and staged rollout policies. The gateway will act as a control-plane component that evaluates a candidate runtime/model image against the target channel's stability requirements before permitting rollout. Goals: (1) reduce incidents caused by upgrades to LTS channels, (2) catch regressions earlier with realistic traffic shadowing, (3) provide deterministic gating logic configurable per-channel.
acceptance_criteria: The validation gateway can run a smoke test matrix against a candidate release using live traffic shadowing for 1h and produce a pass/fail report.
Perf gate: end-to-end 99p latency and tail token throughput measured; regression threshold default <= 5% for non-LTS channels and <= 2% for LTS channels.
Eval suite integration: automated rerun of the standard release-evals collection with per-scenario thresholds; results persisted to the release dashboard.
Ability to attach channel policy that enforces different gate strictness for LTS vs stable vs nightly.
Rollout blocked automatically on critical failures; manual override requires two approvers with audit log entry.
Console view: expose validation artifact links, artifact diffs, and per-check traces in the Release page.
test_plan: Create an isolated shadowing sandbox to mirror 5% of production QPS for test experiments.
Run smoke tests (auth, generation, embeddings, long-run KV scenarios) against 3 model variants and two hardware backends.
Execute perf regression harness collecting token-level latencies and throughput; compare against baseline stored for the target LTS version.
Run evaluation suite (NLG quality + embed similarity + rerank metrics) using the existing eval harness and persist gold references.
Simulate failure modes: KV cache migration issues, model-load OOM, degraded kernel fallback — validate rollback triggers.
rollout_strategy: Validation Gateway evaluates candidate -> if pass then allow canary rollout to 1% traffic with automatic observation window -> if stable, escalate to staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with LTS channels using stricter perf thresholds and 24h extended canary. Shadowing will run throughout to catch regressions that only appear at scale.
notes: 2025-11-05: Kickoff meeting. Agreed to reuse existing shadow proxy (shadowd) with minor enhancements for sampling by channel. ACTION: infra to add policy tag to sampling logic. -- Aisha

2025-11-06: Implementation plan: gateway will be a controller service wired into release-orchestrator; it will spawn ephemeral validation clusters for heavy evals to avoid impacting shared infra. Trade-off: ephemeral clusters add cost but isolate noise from production. -- Roberto

2025-11-07: Perf threshold discussion in design review: Ops prefers conservative 2% for LTS; Prod suggests 3% to avoid blocking too many releases. Decision: default 2% but make channel-configurable. Documented justification in Confluence. -- Notes link below

2025-11-09: PoC run against runtime-2.0-rc1 with 5% QPS shadowing: smoke tests passed, perf showed 3.8% regression on 95p tail on GPU-A; root cause traced to attention-kernel change. Created PR to revert kernel selection fallback. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821

2025-11-11: UX: Console team prototyped validation artifact drawer. Feedback: show diffs of model config and kernel selection, and allow direct link to failing trace. UX PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/231
2025-11-12: Security review: no new data plane auth changes. Decided to require audit entries for manual overrides. Pending: add KMS audit binding.
risks: Increased infra cost due to ephemeral clusters for heavy evals; mitigation: run large evals during off-peak windows and cap concurrent runs.
False positives on perf gates caused by noisy neighbors; mitigation: require multiple independent windows and compare to baseline percentiles.
Shadowing can expose internal-only endpoints; mitigation: enforce request sanitization and strip PII before forwarding.
Manual override could bypass safety; mitigation: require two approvers and an audit entry recorded in the release log.
